paragraphs: Apple appears ready to make a serious push into the smart home market with a new screen-equipped hub dubbed HomeView. It’s reportedly coming at a product launch event on October 13.
The device is for those who want to put the new Siri AI at the center of their home, as well as those who are serious about Apple’s HomeKit smart home accessories. Or both.
Here’s everything we know about Apple’s smart home hub in the days before it is expected to launch.

Apple has a long history of not being first to market. It did not make the original MP3 player, smartphone or wireless headphones, but these were all niche products before Apple took the iPod, iPhone and AirPods mainstream. That appears to be the plan with the HomeView smart home hub.
The rival Google Nest Hub offers the Google Assistant and control of compatible smart-home devices. Amazon Echo Show devices take a similar approach, combining Alexa with smart-home controls.

These competing hubs have been on the market for years, but neither is as popular as smartphones, tablets or even basic smart speakers. Apple’s offering might be the breakthrough product the category is missing.

Every new product category needs an easy-to-understand selling point. And for Apple’s smart home hub, that’s apparently Siri AI. This digital assistant is available on the iPhone and other devices, but the goal of the new device seems to be: Make Siri ubiquitous.

Someone can interact with a hub sitting on a countertop or hanging on a wall simply by talking — without needing to grab another device. The user could, for example, ask Siri to display their calendar, then add an event without ever touching the hub. Or they could use the home hub to look up a recipe.
